roles.name: Attorney under an enduring power of attorney
roles.summary: An attorney for legal and financial affairs whose power continues after the principal loses mental capacity. The instrument must say so, and must be witnessed and certified by a prescribed witness such as a lawyer or Local Court registrar. The attorney has no authority until they accept by signing. The prescribed form lets the principal choose when it operates, including only once a doctor certifies incapacity.

assigned.event: Principal signs an instrument expressed to continue despite loss of capacity. A prescribed witness (not an attorney) witnesses it and certifies they explained it and the principal appeared to understand.

starts.event: When the attorney accepts by signing (at execution or later), and then from the commencement chosen in the form: on acceptance (default), once a medical practitioner considers the principal unable to manage their affairs, once the attorney considers help is needed, or another event

ends.event: Revocation by the principal while they have capacity. Once NCAT or the Supreme Court declares the principal incapable, the principal cannot lawfully revoke.
Revoked in whole or part by NCAT or the Supreme Court on review
Suspended while the principal's estate is under a financial management order (managed estate), unless the Tribunal keeps it in force for excluded property. The Supreme Court may terminate it.

Vacancy of the only attorney (death, resignation, bankruptcy, loss of capacity or revocation of the attorney), or of one joint attorney unless the instrument provides otherwise and a substitute exists

Death of the principal. There is no express termination section: the rule comes from general law, which the Act assumes (only irrevocable powers are saved from death by s 16) and which NSW Government guidance states.
Bankruptcy of the principal (general law; the Act says so only indirectly, by saving irrevocable powers from bankruptcy)

notes.text: Registration is optional (General Register of Deeds). It is required only before a conveyance or other deed affecting land made under the power can have effect; leases of 3 years or less are excluded. The citation is POA Act s 52, not Conveyancing Act s 163B, which is the predecessor provision.

An attorney who acts without knowing of termination, and a third party who deals in good faith without knowing of it, are protected. Acting with knowledge of termination is an offence carrying up to 5 years imprisonment.
An enduring attorney cannot make health or lifestyle decisions; those belong to an enduring guardian or tribunal-appointed guardian.

roles.name: Enduring guardian
roles.summary: A person an adult appoints, by a witnessed instrument the appointee also accepts, to make decisions about where they live, health care, personal services and consent to medical and dental treatment. The appointment operates only while the appointor is a 'person in need of a guardian'. It is revoked automatically if the appointor later marries someone else, and is suspended by any guardianship order.

assigned.event: Adult (18+) signs prescribed-form instrument; appointee endorses acceptance; eligible witness certifies voluntary execution and apparent understanding

starts.event: Only while the appointor is totally or partially incapable of managing their person because of a disability. The appointee may ask NCAT to declare that the appointment has effect.

ends.event: Revocation by the appointor with legal capacity, by prescribed witnessed instrument with written notice to the appointee
Appointor marries or remarries someone other than the appointee
Resignation: by written notice if the appointor is not in need of a guardian, or with Tribunal approval if they are
Revocation by NCAT on review (best interests or at the guardian's request) or by the Supreme Court
Appointor regains capacity: the appointment stops having effect, but revives in any later period of need
Death of the appointor

notes.text: A guardianship order automatically suspends all the enduring guardian's authority for as long as the order lasts. A person already under a guardianship order cannot validly appoint an enduring guardian.
A substitute enduring guardian acts only if the original guardian dies or resigns, or while the original guardian is incapacitated.
Section 6A has no separate commencement trigger such as a medical certificate. Whether the appointor is in need of a guardian is a question of fact, and NCAT can make a declaration.

roles.name: Financial manager under a financial management order
localNames: NSW Trustee and Guardian (as financial manager)
roles.summary: If NCAT finds a person not capable of managing their affairs, that someone needs to manage them, and that an order is in the person's best interests, it puts the estate under management. It appoints a private manager, who acts under Supreme Court directions or NSW Trustee authorisation, or commits management to the NSW Trustee. Any power of attorney is suspended while the estate is managed. Management ends at death.

localNames: executor to whom probate has been granted
roles.summary: The person named in the will. When the Supreme Court grants probate, the deceased's NSW property vests in the executor as from the date of death. roles.name: NSW Trustee administering a small estate without a grant
roles.summary: NSW has no general affidavit procedure that lets family collect a small estate without a grant. Only the NSW Trustee has statutory small-estate powers: it may file an election to administer instead of seeking a grant, deal with an estate as if it held a grant after giving notice, or pay small sums it owes to a deceased person without administration. All thresholds are 'prescribed by the regulations'. Private institutions' release-without-probate thresholds are their own policy.

roles.name: Senior available next of kin (tissue donation)
roles.summary: NSW is opt-in. If the deceased gave unrevoked written consent, a hospital designated officer may authorise removal on that basis. Otherwise, provided the deceased had not objected, the senior available next of kin may consent: spouse or de facto partner, then adult child, then parent, then adult sibling. No next of kin of the same or higher class may object.

assigned.event: By operation of law under the s 4 definition at death

starts.event: On death, where the deceased's own written consent is not established

ends.event: Removal authorised or not pursued. Consent is barred if the deceased objected (and the objection was not later withdrawn) or if equal- or higher-ranked next of kin object.

notes.text: The Australian Organ Donor Register is the national register where people 16 and over record a donation decision. Its legal effect in NSW works through the Human Tissue Act consent provisions; no statutory link was verified.
Special rules apply to deceased children and to children in the care of the State (ss 23A, 24A).

roles.name: Person entitled to arrange disposal of the body
roles.summary: No NSW statute sets a general order of priority. At common law the executor (or the person with the highest right to administration) is said to control disposal (Smith v Tamworth City Council); this is not verified from a primary source here. For cremation, the Public Health Regulation 2022 lets an executor or a nearest surviving relative apply. A medical referee must refuse a permit if cremation would go against the deceased's written direction.

poaDurableByDefault.note: A power of attorney endures only if it is expressed to continue despite loss of capacity and is certified by a prescribed witness. The general form ceases on loss of capacity.

springingPoaAllowed.note: Prescribed Form 2 lets the principal choose when the power operates: on acceptance (default), once a medical practitioner considers the principal unable to manage their affairs, once the attorney considers help is needed, or 'Other'. The Act's only statutory gate is the attorney's acceptance (s 20).

poaRegistrationBeforeUse.note: Registration is optional, except that a conveyance or deed affecting land under a power has no effect until the power is registered (leases of 3 years or less excluded). Citation: POA Act s 52, not Conveyancing Act s 163B.

healthAgentStartsOn.note: An enduring guardian's appointment has effect only while the appointor is a 'person in need of a guardian'. No clinician certificate is required, and NCAT may declare that the appointment has effect.

supportedDecisionMakingStatute.name: None. NSWLRC Report 145 (2018) recommended a new Assisted Decision-Making Act to replace the Guardianship Act 1987 and POA Act Part 4. Law-reform context only; not enacted in the current Guardianship Act.

digitalAssetsFiduciaryStatute.name: None enacted. NSWLRC Report 147 (2019) recommended a statutory scheme for access to digital records on death or incapacity. No such provision found in NSW in-force legislation.

organDonationModel.name: Human Tissue Act 1983 (NSW): the deceased's written consent, or consent of the senior available next of kin absent objection. Decisions can be recorded on the national Australian Organ Donor Register.

smallEstateWithoutGrant.note: No general procedure lets a relative or affiant collect a small estate without a grant. The statutory small-estate powers belong to the NSW Trustee alone (NTGA ss 18, 26, 31), with amounts 'prescribed by the regulations'; the exact figures could not be read from the regulation (see unverified). The old Probate and Administration Act Div 2A (ss 61A–61F) was repealed in 2009. Banks' release-without-probate limits are institutional policy.

probateGrantName.note: The Supreme Court of NSW grants probate (executor) or letters of administration (administrator).

deceasedPersonalDataProtected.note: The Commonwealth Privacy Act does not protect deceased persons (see au-commonwealth). The NSW Health Records and Information Privacy Act 2002 excludes information only once the person has been dead for more than 30 years, so NSW health information stays protected for 30 years after death.

healthAgentPostDeathAuthority.note: An enduring guardian's appointment operates only while the appointor is in need of a guardian. NSW Government guidance says a guardian's role ceases at death. Body disposal and estate matters pass to the executor or administrator.
